findings.title: Set operations cause duplicate column errors
findings.scenario: When UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT combines two branches projecting the same column name (e.g., both selecting event_type), the build step at line 989 attempts SELECT [*] on a combined expression, causing Ibis to raise Duplicate column name event_type in result set. This blocks any set-operation query with overlapping projection columns.
findings.fix: The _apply_set_ops function needs to explicitly rename/alias duplicate columns from right branch before appending to left, or the select-item dispatch should deduplicate column names during set-op assembly. Check _star_columns and _apply_set_ops for the dedup logic that already exists and ensure it runs for set ops too.

findings.title: DISTINCT before set operations fails
findings.scenario: When DISTINCT is placed before a UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT, the build step at line 946 tries to resolve column name against frames that only contain the first branch's tables, raising PayloadError unknown column. DISTINCT after set operations works correctly.
findings.fix: The build function needs to handle DISTINCT at the pipeline level after set operations are resolved, or move DISTINCT processing to occur after _apply_set_ops completes rather than during _build.

findings.title: DuckDB engine rejects savepoints
findings.scenario: Calling savepoint on a DuckDB backed connection raises PayloadError the duckdb engine has no savepoints it keeps whole transactions begin commit rollback. The tx.py functions all delegate to savepoint_statement which calls statement, and DuckDB throws TransactionException for transaction nesting. This is deliberate engine behavior, but the error message and API surface are misleading if callers expect savepoint support.
findings.fix: Either add a clear warning to the docstring of savepoint/rollback_to/release that DuckDB does not support savepoints, or make tx.py engine-aware and skip/no-op savepoint operations when the engine is DuckDB.

findings.title: Temporal year alone is not grouped; with GROUP BY it becomes a grouping key
findings.scenario: When year timestamp is used without GROUP BY, it produces row-wise extraction. When used with GROUP BY year, the extracted part becomes a derived grouping column and the query correctly groups by it. The TEMPORAL_FNS check in build keys off dtype families.
findings.fix: Document the behavioral difference year without GROUP BY row-wise extraction; year with GROUP BY grouping key. The existing tests already document this boundary.

findings.title: Scalar subquery requires explicit alias
findings.scenario: Writing select without an alias in SELECT raises PayloadError a scalar subquery needs an alias write . The consumer must write select as subname. This is a contract constraint.
findings.fix: Improve the error message to show the exact syntax Scalar subquery must be aliased write (SELECT ...) as name.

findings.title: Like operator uses CONTAINS internally
findings.scenario: The like operator compiles to SQL CONTAINS t0 path /P/ rather than SQL LIKE. This means trailing wildcards behave differently. Users expecting standard SQL LIKE may be surprised.
findings.fix: Either document the CONTAINS vs LIKE semantic difference, or adjust the compile path to use standard LIKE.

findings.title: Regex operator requires string column type
findings.scenario: Using where user_id ~ 1 raises PayloadError needs a string column user_id is int64. The regex match operation only works on string-typed columns.
findings.fix: This is correct type-gate behavior. No fix needed unless we want to auto-cast.

findings.title: temp table namespace targeting
findings.scenario: Temp table names are qualified as tempmainname via _temp_name. This ensures temp names cannot reach persistent tables, but also means temp table names are engine-scoped. For DuckDB, this always produces tempmainname prefix.
findings.fix: No fix needed this is working as designed the temp namespace isolation is intentional.

findings.title: count with empty input returns 0 rows
findings.scenario: When from events select count as n limit 0 is executed against the events dataset, the result has 0 rows and 1 column [n]. This is because the limit 0 cuts before any rows are produced.
findings.fix: No fix needed this is correct behavior per the pipeline.

findings.title: Pipeline order matches documented flow
findings.scenario: The engine pipeline order sourcejoins filter projectionaggregation set ops distinct order limit matches the documented invariant. All probed queries confirm this ordering is correct and consistent.
findings.fix: No fix needed this is verified correct.

glue_notes: The engine layer couples to the query layer via the payload dict format dataset select where groupBy orderBy limit setOps distinct unionintersectexcept. The critical seams are: 1 expression.build expects payload from payload_from_ast parse_query any deviation raw dict with wrong keys causes PayloadError at multiple entry points 2 tx create_temp temp_handle drop_temp couple the execution layer to connection level temp namespaces tempmainname which is the only persistence mechanism besides the in memory registry 3 the build compile execute pipeline is pure no state written back into the document matching the repo invariants. The tx execute coupling is loose execute calls build then expr execute while materialize also calls build then tx create_temp both paths are orthogonal to the document state. No data leakage observed.
summary: BRIEF B engine layer probe complete 9 findings across severity levels 1 High set op dedup 1 Medium DISTINCT placement 1 Medium DuckDB savepoint rejection 3 Low temporal grouping scalar subquery alias like CONTAINS semantics 3 Nit Nit adjacent regex type gate temp namespace count empty input. All findings are patch anchored at specific file line ranges and confirmed via read only probes against the demo DuckDB connection. No repo files were modified.
